Theorem 5.22. Every path is either a row or a column and a path contains at most one
quantum operator. Paths can be cyclically shifted to a classical row or to a classical column.
The only path that can be shifted to both consists of a single operator.
Proof. We split the proof into four parts. Let v be a path, which is nonzero.
(1) Paths consisting only of classical operators. Suppose the path v = varbr · · ·va1b1 is a
composition of classical operators (for all i, ai < bi). Then every pair of adjacent compositions
vai+1,bi+1vai,bi is nonzero. Suppose that a1 is an endpoint. As v̸ ≡0, the relations (5.1)(ii)
imply that ai+1 = bi for all i. Similarly, if b1 is an endpoint, then we must have ai = bi+1
for all i. Thus, v is either a connected classical row or a connected classical column. If
v = varbr · · · va1b1 with for example, ai < bi and ai+1 = bi for all i, then we showed that
v̸ ≡0, and so v is a connected classical row. If instead ai = bi+1, then applying ρ or w0
shows that v is a connected classical column. Such paths are shown in (5.5) in Figure 15.

the path v = varar−1 · · · va2a1va1b · vba is a composition of a connected classical column
